claim: Gene-expression profiles measured at diagnosis predict survival time in new patients: the out-of-sample R-squared for predicting survival_months from the expression profile is at least 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: log2 expression level of each gene in each patient's tumour sample
months from diagnosis to death, observed for every patient

claim: Within patients, oxygen consumption rises with oxygen delivery: the mean over patients of the within-patient slope of oxygen consumption on oxygen delivery is at least 0.1 mL/min per mL/min.

data_keys.meaning: cardiac output of each patient at each measurement occasion, in L/min
oxygen content of arterial blood of each patient at each occasion, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen content of mixed venous blood of each patient at each occasion, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen consumption of each patient at each occasion measured from expired-gas analysis, in mL/min

claim: The postal district and the three covariates together predict the outcome y for new patients: the Pearson correlation between predicted and observed y is at least 0.25.

data_keys.meaning: True where the patient's home postal district is the district of that column
three continuous covariates per patient (age, body-mass index, systolic pressure)
continuous health outcome of each patient

claim: Gene-expression profiles distinguish the two leukaemia types in new samples: the area under the ROC curve is at least 0.90.

data_keys.meaning: expression level of each gene in each bone-marrow sample
True for acute myeloid leukaemia, False for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia

claim: In a field experiment, 10 plots were each surveyed at 30 quadrats and each quadrat was scored as occupied or not by a seaweed species; the array exclosure marks plots fenced against grazers. Claim: mean occupancy is higher in fenced plots than in open plots by at least 0.10, where the occupancy of a plot is the fraction of its quadrats that are occupied, and a one-sided test of the difference between the mean occupancy of fenced plots and that of open plots is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: True if the species was present in that quadrat of that plot
True if the plot was fenced against grazers

claim: A second-order polynomial regression of the quality score y on the process readings X (an intercept, the 10 readings, their squares and all pairwise products, fitted by ordinary least squares) predicts y for new runs with a Pearson correlation between predicted and observed y of at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: 10 continuous process readings recorded for each production run
continuous quality score of each production run

claim: Across 2000 adult specimens of one beetle species, head width and wing length are associated beyond what body length explains: the partial correlation between head width and wing length, controlling for body length, is at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: head width of each specimen, in mm
wing length of each specimen, in mm
body length of each specimen, in mm

claim: The 25 measurements in X predict the outcome y for new samples: the mean absolute error of an ordinary least squares regression of y on X (with an intercept) is at least 10% below that of predicting the mean of y: 1 - MAE(model) / MAE(mean predictor) >= 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: 25 continuous measurements for each sample
continuous outcome of each sample

claim: A classifier built from the measured variables recognises both classes in new records: the balanced accuracy (the mean of sensitivity and specificity for the positive class) is at least 0.65.

data_keys.meaning: measured variables of each record
True if the condition is present in the record

claim: Across skulls, cranial breadth and cranial height are positively associated after accounting for cranial length: the partial correlation coefficient between breadth and height, given length, is at least 0.2.

data_keys.meaning: maximum cranial breadth of each skull, in mm
cranial height of each skull, in mm
maximum cranial length of each skull, in mm

claim: A nearest-neighbour regression (one neighbour, Euclidean distance on standardised descriptors) of the response y on the descriptors X predicts y for new compounds with a Pearson correlation between predicted and observed y of at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: 20 continuous molecular descriptors recorded for each compound record
continuous activity response measured for each compound record

claim: 600 patients with menopausal hot flushes received a treatment. Symptom severity (scale 0 to 100, higher is worse) was scored at a screening visit, again at entry on the day treatment began, and again 12 weeks later. Claim: among patients whose screening score was at least 60, at least half have a week-12 score that is 10 or more points below their entry score (proportion of at least 0.5).

data_keys.meaning: symptom severity score at the screening visit
symptom severity score at entry, on the day treatment began
symptom severity score 12 weeks after treatment began
